content.intro: This lesson covers Choosing Between Loops, Iterators, and Functional Operations. It sits in Module 4, Operators and Control Flow, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Choosing Between Loops, Iterators, and Functional Operations matters when you work with capturing values and transforming sequences. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Iterators describe a sequence of values and compose transformations. Many adaptors are lazy, so a terminal operation such as collect, sum, or for_each is needed to consume the sequence.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Choosing Between Loops, Iterators, and Functional Operations, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. if is an expression, for ranges are often the clearest bounded loop, and iterator pipelines can express transformations without manual index management.
